context_scope.population: Masked WorldPop statistic supplies exposure context, not measured harm or universal peak exposure.
context_scope.precipitation_products: 2015-03-01 to 2015-04-15 early-window context; useful for background moisture checks but not a complete 2015-2016 drought index.
context_scope.remote_sensing: MODIS/VIIRS preview supports fire, smoke, air-quality, and drought-stress monitoring context; it is not a standalone burn-scar attribution.

key_values.event_name: 2015-2016 El Nino and Indonesian drought/fire haze

rejected_alternatives.cyclone_or_coastal_surge: No cyclone, wind-surge, or coastal-inundation mechanism explains the ONI, peat, haze, CO, and PSI chain.
rejected_alternatives.heat_only_response: Heat may accompany drought, but the supported impact pathway is smoke-haze air quality and transport disruption.
rejected_alternatives.heavy_rain_flooding: The decisive record is seasonal El Nino dryness, peat fire, smoke chemistry, and PSI/CO exceedance rather than damaging rainfall.
rejected_alternatives.image_only_burn_scar: Remote sensing is useful monitoring context, but the priority depends on forecastable dry-weather risk plus peat/fire and air-quality evidence.

primary_gt.action_logic: Use seasonal El Nino and dry-weather warning to trigger peat fire prevention, smoke monitoring, air-quality health protection, and transport disruption preparedness before the haze crisis escalates.
primary_gt.canonical_stance: The 2015-2016 Indonesian crisis is best framed as forecast-triggered peat-fire and haze preparedness driven by strong El Nino dry-weather risk, peat and land-use fire conditions, and severe smoke-related air-quality impacts.

forbidden_claims: exact deaths, illnesses, burned area, or economic losses not supported by the record
El Nino as the sole cause without peat and land-use fire conditions
remote sensing alone as sufficient for the disaster mechanism
flood, cyclone or coastal surge as the primary operational frame

required_claims: strong sustained El Nino provides a forecastable dry-weather driver
peat and land-use fire conditions convert the climate anomaly into smoke and haze
air-quality indicators show severe smoke exposure and transport disruption
preparedness should begin before haze conditions escalate
flood, cyclone or surge, heat-only, and image-only interpretations are not primary

criteria.description: Selects forecast-triggered peat-fire haze preparedness or a semantically equivalent priority and gives a three-part mechanism linking El Nino dry-weather forcing, peat or land-use fire conditions, and regional smoke-haze air-quality impacts.
criteria.name: Final priority and mechanism label
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for naming fire-haze preparedness without the forecast trigger, or for omitting one mechanism link while preserving the correct hazard.

criteria.description: Reports peak ONI 2.75, nine 2015-2016 seasons at or above 1.5 C, carbon monoxide ratio 13.0, and PSI hazard ratio about 5.7 with correct interpretation.
criteria.name: Quantitative anchors
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for two or three correct metrics, harmless rounding differences, or correct values with weak units.

criteria.description: Explains the teleconnection-to-dry-weather forecast, the one-month preparedness window, and how peat and fire use convert drought stress into persistent smoke.
criteria.name: Physical mechanism reasoning
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for connecting El Nino to fires but not distinguishing driver, fuel condition, and impact pathway.

criteria.description: Integrates climate index, report claims, air-quality thresholds, aerosol and carbon monoxide indicators, bounded precipitation context, exposure context, and satellite-monitoring context without over-weighting one source.
criteria.name: Cross-scale evidence fusion
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for using only climate plus one impact metric or treating imagery as merely illustrative.

criteria.description: Recommends early peat-fire prevention, smoke monitoring, public-health protection, and transport disruption preparedness before escalation.
criteria.name: Operational action logic
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for generic emergency response recommendations that do not target haze or preparedness timing.

criteria.description: Explains why flood, cyclone or surge, heat-only, and image-only interpretations are not primary, and avoids unsupported mortality, loss, burned-area, or legal blame claims.
criteria.name: Rejection of competing explanations and overclaims
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for rejecting some alternatives while missing others, or for one minor unsupported escalation.

criteria.description: Returns compact JSON in the requested structure, including context_scope, rejected_alternatives, and a concise action sentence.
criteria.name: Output discipline
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for readable structured output with minor schema deviations.
